summary: Dhal puri roti, Caribbean lentil-stuffed flatbread: a dough of all-purpose and whole-wheat pastry flours rested 1 hour, filled with a spiced split pea puree, rolled to about 10 inches and cooked about 1 1/2 minutes per side in butter on a griddle; makes 12, 1 hour 15 minutes active (2 1/2 hours total).
glance: rest 1 hour, then 30 more minutes in balls
1 1/2 cups yellow split peas, 3 tablespoons per bread
about 1 1/2 minutes per side on a medium griddle
faq: What is dhal puri roti?

A Caribbean flatbread variation made on many islands that originated with Indian immigrants. The name can seem confusing because in Indian terminology a poori and a roti are two different breads. They are quite filling: a small side-dish curry and a little rice make a complete meal.
Why use whole-wheat pastry flour?
The author uses about 50 percent: it's more nutritious than white flour and adds a more complex flavor, and being lower in gluten it helps keep the bread tender.
How do I make the filling?

Saute onion and garlic, add the split peas and 6 cups of water, simmer until easily crushed between your fingers but not turning into soup, drain, and pulse in a food processor with oil, turmeric, cumin, cayenne and salt, coarsely pureed with a bit of texture. It should form a ball but not be bone-dry; too wet makes the roti soggy.
How do I fill and roll them?
Roll a ball of dough to about 5 inches, put 3 tablespoons of filling in the center, pull the edges up and seal to enclose completely, flatten and roll to about 10 inches and less than 1/4 inch thick.
Can I make them ahead?
Yes, they reheat beautifully in the microwave, but they are best steaming hot because otherwise the filling can be dry.
How should they be cooked?
Lightly browned on each side in a little butter on a skillet or griddle at least 12 inches wide; you don't want them crispy, the bread should remain soft.

summary: Chermoula-stuffed eggplant: globe eggplant halves slit into a pocket, rubbed with chermoula (a North African herb sauce), brushed with oil and baked at 450°F about 30 minutes until tender, then finished with more fresh chermoula and feta; serves 4, 20 minutes active plus 30 in the oven.
glance: 20 minutes active plus 30 minutes in the oven
450°F until completely tender and just starting to brown, about 30 minutes
2 medium globe (about 14 ounces each), halved and cut into a pocket
faq: What is chermoula?
A sort of North African pesto of herbs and spices; here it bakes into the creamy eggplant flesh, seasoning it.
Why add more chermoula at the end?
So you enjoy both the cooked and fresh flavors of the herbs and spices: some is rubbed in before baking and the rest drizzled on just before serving.
How do I cut the pocket?

Trim about 1/8 inch off two opposing sides for a stable surface, halve lengthwise, then cut each half almost in half again lengthwise, leaving it attached for the last 1/2 inch at the base. Open it and rub the inside with a generous tablespoon of chermoula, then close it back up.
Is it a main dish?
Not a large entree: serve it with generous quantities of couscous and chickpeas or a rice pilaf, yogurt and salad.
How do I bake it?
Place on a generously oiled baking sheet wide side up, brush the tops with olive oil, season with salt, and bake at 450°F about 30 minutes. Finish with the remaining chermoula and crumbled feta.

summary: Tomato and nectarine salad with a Korean dressing: perfectly ripe heirloom tomato wedges and nectarine segments with arugula, sweet onion and flaky salt, dressed with grapeseed oil, toasted sesame oil, gochugaru and sherry vinegar; serves 4 and only worth making with spectacular fruit.
glance: 2-3 large perfectly ripe heirloom tomatoes and 3 ripe nectarines (or peaches), at room temperature
1/4 cup grapeseed oil, 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, 1/4 to 1 teaspoon fine gochugaru, 2 tablespoons sherry vinegar
faq: Why combine tomatoes and nectarines?

Pairing tomatoes with fruit plays on the fact that tomatoes are a fruit, emphasizing their sweetness and complex flavors. Stone fruit and tomato salads are on many great restaurant menus. It's only worth doing with spectacular heirloom tomatoes and nectarines; hard pink tomatoes and underripe nectarines will be tasteless.
What is gochugaru?
A Korean chili powder. The author's is fruity and sour and not particularly spicy, but taste yours first and dial it back if hot. If you don't have it, try ancho chili powder or a pinch of cayenne.
Where does the dressing come from?
The author wanted a simple first course to serve before icy cold Korean noodles (jjolmyeon).
Do I have to plate it fancy?
No, guests will enjoy it just as much family style. Fancy plating uses just a few arugula leaves; family style uses a couple of cups and you can skip the cherry tomatoes.
How do I cut the nectarines?
Into segments. If they are clingstones you'll lose some of the flesh, but you can gnaw on the pit as a cook's treat; freestone is preferable.

summary: Raspberry-blueberry buckle, a rustic baked fruit dessert based on a Joy of Cooking recipe: a whole wheat pastry flour cake batter with 3 cups of fresh berries folded in and a nutmeg streusel, baked at 350°F in a 9x9 pan for about 40 minutes; serves 8.
glance: 350°F for about 40 minutes, until browned and a toothpick comes out clean
faq: What is a buckle?

A rustic American baked fruit dessert in the same family as cobblers, crisps, crumbles, grunts and slumps: a quick cake batter mixed with fresh fruit, topped with streusel and baked. The name apparently comes from how the streusel top buckles (bends and cracks) in the oven.
What fruit can I use?
Any fruit that could live in a pie: pitted cherries, pears, peaches, apples, even pineapple. It will seem like too much fruit, but fold it in gently.
Which flour is best?

You can use cake flour or all-purpose, but the author's favorite is whole wheat pastry flour: it's low in gluten so the crumb is tender, with a little bonus nutrition without any overt signs of being health food.
How do I serve it?
Cool for 20 minutes and serve while still warm, with vanilla ice cream or a pour of heavy cream.
How do I make the streusel?
Mix sugar, flour, nutmeg and salt, work in 4 tablespoons of cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse cornmeal, and refrigerate until ready; a few larger bits of butter are fine.

summary: Fresh spinach fettuccine with goat cheese, Jerusalem artichokes, morels and leeks: a cream and garlic reduction melted with chevre, sauteed sunchoke slices, rehydrated morels and baby leeks, tossed with fresh pasta cooked about 3 minutes; a blueprint for fresh pasta dishes, serves 4.
glance: 1.5 pounds fresh spinach fettuccine, about 3 minutes
3/4 cup heavy cream and 6 cloves garlic reduced by half, whisked with 1 pound chevre
1.5 pounds Jerusalem artichokes, 1.5 ounces dried morels, leeks
faq: Do dried morels work?

Morels are one of the few mushrooms that really survive drying and rehydrating well; if anything the taste becomes more concentrated. Soak 1.5 ounces in just barely boiling water, drain, and save the soaking liquid, which is delicious.
What are Jerusalem artichokes?

Also called sunchokes, tubers that the author peels, slices 1/4 inch thick and sautes in a very hot skillet with plenty of olive oil for a sweet caramelized exterior with a satisfying crunch. Reading Harold McGee's The Curious Cook, he learned they cause gas, reduced by boiling them a while in plenty of water, which he didn't do.
What sauce pairs with fresh pasta?

Generally speaking, fresh pastas like cream-based sauces better than tomato-based ones. Here cream is reduced with garlic and the goat cheese melted in; alternatively dress the noodles with olive oil or butter and leave the chevre in chunks.
Why season each component?
The author stresses salting each component to taste instead of waiting until the end or relying on the sauce: you get a much better dish.
How do I clean leeks?
Remove all but the white part, slice in half lengthwise and wash carefully, since there tends to be dirt between the leaves; then slice thin.

summary: The "inside-out egg," an April Fools-style joke dessert that is really mango and coconut: mango puree set with agar-agar in plastic Easter egg molds around a spoonful of coconut cream, with the halves glued together with more agar and chilled 15 minutes; makes 4.
glance: 4 plastic Easter eggs that split in half
250 ml mango puree with 1 teaspoon agar-agar, boiled and set 15 minutes
the creamy top of an unshaken can of full-fat coconut milk
faq: Is the inside-out egg real?

It looks like one, but it was a joke the author published as the real thing: it's actually made from mango set with agar-agar and coconut cream, molded in a plastic Easter egg. Some readers believed it or thought it was an unborn egg.
How do I make the egg?

Spray plastic Easter egg halves with cooking spray and stand them upright. Boil the mango puree, whisk in agar for 20 seconds, turn off the heat, whisk 30 more seconds, pour into the molds and chill 15 minutes (agar sets really fast). Fill hollows with coconut cream, brush the rims with boiling agar water, press the halves together and chill 15 more minutes.
How do I get the coconut cream?
Without shaking, open the can of full-fat coconut milk and spoon out the creamy part at the top; reserve the liquid for another recipe.
What agar should I use?
Agar-agar powder, not the pre-sweetened kind.
Has anyone made something similar?
The author mentions a similar dish on Top Chef made with panna cotta and right-side out, and a tomato and mozzarella version in Michel Richard's Happy in the Kitchen.

summary: Grilled pineapple salsa: half a fresh pineapple sliced into 3/8-inch planks, brushed with oil and grilled over medium-high heat until dark grill marks form, diced and mixed with lime juice, shallot, jalapeno, cilantro and salt; makes about 1.5 cups in about 15 minutes.
glance: medium-high heat until dark grill marks develop on each side
faq: Why cut my own pineapple?
Pre-cut pineapple is in chunks too small to grill effectively. Remove the skin entirely and slice into vertical planks about 3/8 inch thick; you only need half a pineapple for this recipe.
Do I need a grill?
If you have one going for other reasons, use it. Otherwise a cast-iron grill pan with a ridged side works well.
How long should I grill the pineapple?
Long enough to drive off some moisture and develop caramelized flavors: brush each side with canola oil and a little salt and grill until dark grill marks develop.
Can I make it ahead?
If not using right away, hold off on the cilantro so it stays bright. Taste and adjust salt, lime juice and heat.
What does it go with?
Tacos, or a Southeast Asian context, especially with lemongrass and/or ginger; the author also eats it with chips at midnight.

summary: White bean and kale soup built on the beans' own cooking liquid, with a parmesan rind, dried porcini or vegetarian broth powder for umami: beans pressure-cooked 40 minutes (or simmered on the stovetop), then lacinato kale and lemon juice simmered 10 minutes; makes 10 cups and serves 6.
glance: 20 minutes active; 1 1/2 hours total with a pressure cooker
2 cups dry cannellini, pressure cooked 40 minutes with 7 cups water
a parmesan rind, 3/4 ounce dried porcini, or 2 tablespoons vegetarian broth powder
Gluten-free; vegan option (skip the parmesan rind)
faq: How is the broth built?

The bean cooking liquid is an integral part of the broth. Three options add umami: a parmesan rind (the author saves them in the freezer when too hard to grate), dried porcini mushrooms, or vegetarian broth powder; use two if you like.
Do I need a pressure cooker?

If you have one, make the whole soup in it, including the beans. Otherwise do it on the stovetop with more planning: soak and cook the beans as usual, reserving 7 cups of cooking liquid, saute the vegetables, add the bean broth and aromatics and simmer 30 minutes, then add the beans and kale.
How do I cook the kale?
Remove the bay leaves and parmesan rind, add the lacinato kale ribbons (stems stripped, washed) and lemon juice and simmer 10 minutes until thoroughly tender.
How do I make it vegan?
Skip the parmesan rind and use porcini or broth powder for the umami.
What do I garnish with?
A generous drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil.

summary: Cucumber and dill soup (tarator), a chilled Bulgarian yogurt soup from the author's wife's cousin Sabi: finely diced cucumbers with vinegar, olive oil, garlic, chives, mint and dill stirred into a quart of yogurt and a pint of sour cream and chilled at least an hour; serves 6-8, 20 minutes active.
glance: 20 minutes active plus 1 hour to chill
4 cups low-fat yogurt and 2 cups low-fat sour cream
dill, mint and chives or green onions
faq: What is tarator?

The Bulgarian name for this refreshing yogurt-based soup. The recipe comes from the author's wife's cousin Sabi, an Israeli whose family emigrated from Bulgaria. The author's family adds mint and chives to the traditional dill.
How much garlic should I use?
Sabi's recipe calls for 4 cloves, but the author finds 1 or 2 just right. If you make it a day in advance, remember the garlic will grow in strength.
Should I chop or puree the cucumbers?
The author prefers the traditional hand-chopped (about 1/8-inch cubes, seeded, peeled only if the peel is tough) while his wife likes them peeled and pureed in the food processor. Try both.
How do I adjust the texture?
After chilling at least an hour, check it: if very thick stir in a little cold water; if too thin add a little more sour cream. Taste and adjust again, and chill the serving bowls too.
When is it best?
On a hot summer day when you don't want to heat up the kitchen.

summary: A guest recipe from Kathy Strahs of Panini Happy: sharp cheddar and apple butter panini on buttered rosemary bread with rosemary-cayenne candied pecans baked 30 minutes at 300°F; 15 minutes prep, 40 cook, 55 total, makes 4 panini.
glance: Prep 15 min, cook 40 min, total 55 min
1 cup chopped, coated in sugar, rosemary, salt and cayenne and baked at 300°F for 30 minutes
8 ounces sharp cheddar and 1/4 cup apple butter on rosemary or country white bread
faq: Who is Kathy Strahs?

The writer of Panini Happy, a blog exploring unexpected uses for the panini maker, from pressing homemade ice cream cones to grilling smashed potatoes to baking mini layer cakes, besides lots of panini.
How does rosemary work in this sandwich?
Kathy uses it two ways to develop complex, intense flavor: rosemary candied pecans for sweet crunch and gentle heat (with cayenne), and buttered rosemary bread for subtle woodsy notes.
How do I make the candied pecans?

Shake sugar, chopped rosemary, coarse salt and cayenne in a bag, toss 1 cup of chopped pecans in whisked egg white and water, transfer with a slotted spoon to the bag and shake to coat, then bake on a foil-lined sheet at 300°F for 30 minutes, stirring after about 15. Cool; she warns they are very addictive.
How do I assemble the panini?

Top a bread slice with 1/4 of the cheese and a few tablespoons of pecans, spread about a tablespoon of apple butter on another slice and place it apple-butter side down to close the sandwich, brush the top with melted butter and grill on a medium-high panini grill.
Where did the idea come from?
Rosemary Apple Butter Grilled Cheese Sandwiches on Framed Cooks, which Kate found at The Professional Palate.
